title: SD-DVQ: Semantic-Driven Data Visualization Query Generation from Speech Queries

problem.claim: Users need to convert speech queries into data visualizations, but existing data visualization tools can require technical skills and speech-to-visualization methods face speech recognition errors and insufficient model generalization.

gap.claim: Existing speech-to-visualization methods do not adequately address speech recognition errors and insufficient model generalization.

contributions.claim: SD-DVQ is a framework for generating semantically consistent natural language queries from speech using schema information.
SD-DVQ improves downstream data visualization query generation through schema filtering and database-feedback-based self-correction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish SD-DVQ from prior ASR-based cascade and completely end-to-end methods by introducing semantic query generation with schema information, schema filtering, and database-feedback-based self-correction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the SpeechNVBench benchmark, SD-DVQ achieves 45.02% exact-match accuracy.
SD-DVQ outperforms the strongest baseline by 5.07 percentage points.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data visualization helps decision-makers understand large amounts of data, but access can require technical skills.
Speech-to-visualization has emerged with the widespread use of voice interfaces.
Existing methods remain limited by speech recognition errors and insufficient model generalization.
SD-DVQ generates semantically consistent queries with schema information and applies schema filtering plus database-feedback-based self-correction.
Experiments on SpeechNVBench report 45.02% exact-match accuracy and a 5.07 percentage-point improvement over the strongest baseline.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses schema information, schema filtering, and database feedback to guide speech-to-visualization query generation.

interpretation.claim: Incorporating structured data context and execution feedback may help constrain generated queries and correct errors.

application.claim: For similar query-generation systems, consider combining semantic intermediate representations with schema-aware filtering and feedback-based correction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these components generalize beyond the reported benchmark or other database and speech conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture or training procedure.
The abstract does not describe the SpeechNVBench dataset composition or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report separate effects of schema filtering and database-feedback-based self-correction.
